text: We will continue to develop Plaid Cymru’s Inspire Wales programme to involve all ages in sporting activity and ensure our people stay fit and healthy.
explanation: This is a negative example verbatim from the codebook: a straightforward programme commitment (sports participation for fitness/health) with purely instrumental language and no moral vocabulary.

text: Values of respect.
explanation: Explicitly invokes 'respect', which the codebook lists as explicit moral vocabulary under clarification (a). Even though fragmentary, it names a moral value rather than a policy instrument.

text: • Waiting lists are not tolerable.
explanation: Uses 'not tolerable', which maps directly onto the codebook's explicit moral vocabulary 'tolerable/intolerable' (clarification a) — a moral evaluation of waiting lists rather than a neutral performance statistic.

text: to ensure an efficient and accessible school bus system for communities across the country.
explanation: Neutral description of a policy instrument (efficient, accessible school bus system). No moral-evaluative vocabulary; fits the negative clarification's 'neutral description of policy instruments'.

text: work with stakeholders to ensure ticket prices at sporting events do not unfairly discriminate against people from low socio economic backgrounds.
explanation: Uses explicit moral vocabulary — 'unfairly discriminate' against people from low socio-economic backgrounds. Both 'unfair' and 'discriminated' are listed in clarification (a) as moral vocabulary.

text: Much of the UK’s language, culture and way of life has been enriched by successive new arrivals over thousands of years.
explanation: A positive descriptive claim about immigration's contribution to language and culture. 'Enriched' is a generic positive adjective without moral-evaluative content (no justice, rights, fairness vocabulary), fitting the negative clarification.

text: The international evidence is clear:
explanation: An empirical/evidentiary framing ('The international evidence is clear') with no moral vocabulary or normative judgment.

text: and free prescriptions and eye tests for the over-60s, without means testing.
explanation: A neutral description of a policy benefit (free prescriptions and eye tests, no means testing). No moral-evaluative language; a policy instrument per the negative clarification.

text: In government, The Nationals will place any money left in this program in the hands of school boards and principals who are best placed to know how and where the priorities for their schools lie.
explanation: Administrative allocation of programme funds to school boards and principals. Purely technocratic/administrative language with no moral content.

text: Revive the National Adult Learning Council and local co-ordinating bodies so that diverse elements of lifelong learning can be linked into one coherent system through which learners can progress.
explanation: Administrative proposal to revive learning councils and coordinate lifelong learning. Instrumental language, no moral vocabulary.

text: And as I’ve mentioned, as a result of our initiative, the Three Strikes legislation was passed.
explanation: A factual claim that legislation was passed as a result of an initiative. No moral evaluation or moral vocabulary.

text: and stop unions looking to restrict their freedom to choose how they want to work.
explanation: Appeals to freedom ('their freedom to choose how they want to work') as a value being protected against restriction. The clarification explicitly states that appeals to freedom/liberty as a value being protected or unjustly restricted are coded 1.

text: Every person, however frail or vulnerable, has a place and a purpose in this world.
explanation: This is a positive example verbatim from the codebook: it affirms the inherent worth of every human being, 'however frail or vulnerable' — a direct moral claim about human dignity.

text: Ensure that all children will be tested in literacy and numeracy at two stages during their primary school education.
explanation: A neutral policy instrument (literacy/numeracy testing at two stages of primary education). No moral vocabulary.

text: - We have one court system
explanation: A factual/descriptive statement about institutional structure ('We have one court system'). No moral-evaluative content.

text: Many new small businesses are started by women.
explanation: A factual/empirical claim about who starts small businesses. No moral vocabulary or normative judgment.

text: Our economy will be thriving, delivering balanced growth with jobs that last in every nation and region.
explanation: An aspirational economic vision ('thriving', 'balanced growth', 'jobs that last'). Fits the negative clarification: generic positive adjectives and aspirational visions lacking moral vocabulary.

text: courts and tribunals that are independent of the government of the day.
explanation: Describes an institutional/structural arrangement (courts independent of government). 'Independent' here is structural, not moral vocabulary; no moral-evaluative language present.

text: While no one should be denied access to the courts, the rule of lawyers threatens our global competitiveness, denies Americans access to the quality of justice they deserve, and puts every small business one lawsuit away from bankruptcy.
explanation: This is a positive example verbatim from the codebook: it invokes justice and moral desert ('the quality of justice they deserve') and the ethical principle that no one should be denied access to the courts.

text: Prioritise the development of high-standard affordable homes by amending and expanding the use of Special Development Zones and / or a new permit scheme.

text: and contribute new technology.
explanation: Neutral, instrumental fragment about contributing technology. No moral content.

text: / and fast, frequent inner-city services.
explanation: Neutral description of transport services. No moral vocabulary.

text: Introduce a competitive new system for how permits are processed for oil and gas exploration.
explanation: A policy instrument for processing oil and gas exploration permits. Technocratic/administrative, no moral vocabulary.

text: Reduce by 50 per cent the rates bills of village shops, pubs and/or garages where they are the last one, two or three remaining in their communities.

text: · further support for back country reafforestation.

text: Employment of New Zealanders wishing to work is our first priority.

text: Develop individual NZ Inc country strategies to grow our exports with key markets.

text: (E.g. N52/N62 from Dundalk to Limerick, via the Midlands as a strategic road corridor)

text: Introduce new incentives for the provision of Affordable Housing.

explanation: A tourism development/website initiative with local authorities. Purely administrative and instrumental, no moral vocabulary.

text: establish comprehensive and transparent reporting requirements.

text: The qualifications gap between the rich and the poor and between Māori and non-Māori must be closed

text: Promote supervised after-school activities in schools and a wide range of positive afterschool options for children.
